title: PowerShell Script Block Containing A Download Command Pattern
detection_hypothesis: If PowerShell is used to retrieve remote content, the logged script block will contain one of the standard download method names together with a URL scheme.

field_semantics.ScriptBlockText: Decoded PowerShell script block text as executed.

collection_prerequisites: Script block logging is enabled through Group Policy or registry configuration.
PowerShell operational log collection is enabled on the endpoint.
expected_collection_gaps: PowerShell version 2 engines do not emit script block logs.
Very large script blocks are split across multiple events.
normalization_assumptions: ScriptBlockText contains the decoded script text as executed.
ingestion_differences: Multi-part script blocks may need reassembly before matching.
Some pipelines strip newlines from ScriptBlockText.
retention_considerations: Script block logging is moderate to high volume; 90 days is a common target.
expected_volume: Moderate on build agents; low on user endpoints.
false_positive_strategy: Benign matches always reference internal endpoints and run under automation accounts. Tune on the destination host inside the script text plus the host role.
tuning_guidance: Exclude the internal artefact repository hostname. Do not exclude the download method names, since they are the behavioural core of the rule.
test_strategy: Positive cases use two different download methods with the synthetic invalid domain. Negative cases keep a download method without a URL and a URL without a download method.
author: Salvatore Mazzaglia
